<skill_content name="measure">
# Skill: measure

# Measure

Spec-driven development framework that organizes AI-assisted software development into structured, trackable units of work.

**Core Rule:**
- **Human docs explain why.** (e.g., `product.md`, `tech-stack.md`)
- **Generated docs describe what currently exists.** (e.g., `generated/architecture.json`, `generated/routes.md`)

## Core Concepts

- **Track**: A high-level unit of work (feature, bug fix, or chore) with its own spec and plan
- **Spec**: Detailed requirements and acceptance criteria (`spec.md`)
- **Plan**: Phased implementation tasks following strict Contract-First and TDD methodology (`plan.md`)
- **Workflow**: Development procedures including TDD, quality gates, and commit guidelines
- **Lessons Learned**: Curated working-memory file (`lessons-learned.md`) capturing architecture decisions, recurring gotchas, useful patterns, and planning insights across tracks
- **Tech Debt Registry**: Bounded working-memory file (`tech-debt.md`) tracking known shortcuts and deferred work with severity and status
- **Universal File Resolution Protocol**: Index-based file lookup that resolves named references (e.g., **Product Definition**) to file paths via `index.md`

### Sprint Mode (optional)

Feature tracks can opt into a lightweight scrum-style format when creating a new track:

- **Spec format choice** in `new-track` §2.2: pick **Story-shaped spec** (user stories with Gherkin acceptance criteria, T-shirt size, priority) or the existing **Classic FR list**.
- **Stories** become first-class units in `spec.md` under a `## Stories` section. Each story uses the Connextra triplet (`As a … I want … So that …`), Gherkin AC, `Estimate: S|M|L|XL`, `Priority: Must|Should|Could`.
- **Sprint metadata** is captured in `metadata.json.sprint = {goal, stories[], demo_notes, retro_ref}` for story-shaped feature tracks only (omitted for bug/chore/classic tracks).
- **Story-aware plans** use `## Phase S<n>: <story title>` headings, one phase per story, preserving the Contract-First sub-task pipeline.
- **Velocity & estimation accuracy** are reported in `status` under Project Health, computed from the last 3 completed feature tracks.

Sprint Mode is fully opt-in and backward-compatible: classic specs, plans, and metadata files continue to work unchanged.

### Graph-Aware Mode (optional)

When a project's Tech Stack includes TypeScript and `build-graph` (from `repo-graph/`) is on PATH with a fresh `graph.db` (<24h mtime), Measure's workflows automatically enrich themselves with structural facts from the codebase knowledge graph:

- **`new-track`** runs a Graph Context Probe in §2.2 (`build-graph stats` + `search` for feature keywords) so questioning batches cite real symbols, and a Blast-Radius Probe in §2.3 (`build-graph callers` for exported symbols) so each plan phase declares its blast radius.
- **`implement`** loads a graph baseline in §3.2 (`build-graph stats` + `inspect` for exported symbols in the spec/plan), and applies a Per-Task Graph Protocol in §3.3: pre-edit `inspect` records caller count in the commit; post-edit `update` keeps the graph fresh whenever signatures, imports/exports, schemas, or JSX hierarchy change.
- **`review`** loads `build-graph callers` for every changed exported symbol in §2.2 and flags **High**-severity findings in §2.3 when a non-additive signature change is not accompanied by caller updates. `Graph Caller Check: [Pass/Fail/Skipped]` appears in the §2.5 report block.
- **`setup`** §2.9 offers (TS-detected only) to install build-graph, scan the project, and add the standard rules to `AGENTS.md`.

Graph-Aware Mode is fully opt-in: every step emits a one-line `Note: …` and continues if `build-graph` is missing, `graph.db` is stale/absent, or the project isn't TypeScript. No HALT, no breakage.

## Directory Structure

```
measure/
├── index.md                # Index for file resolution
├── product.md              # Product vision and features (Product Definition)
├── product-guidelines.md   # Brand, voice, and design guidelines (Product Guidelines)
├── tech-stack.md           # Technology choices and rationale (Tech Stack)
├── workflow.md             # Development workflow and quality gates (Workflow)
├── tracks.md               # Master list of all tracks (Tracks Registry)
├── lessons-learned.md      # Curated project memory (bounded, 50-line max)
├── tech-debt.md            # Known shortcuts and deferred work (bounded, 50-line max)
├── code_styleguides/       # Language-specific style guides
├── generated/              # Machine-generated facts (architecture.json, routes.md)
├── tracks/                 # Individual track directories
│   └── <track_id>/
│       ├── metadata.json   # Track metadata (incl. optional sprint object for story-shaped feature tracks)
│       ├── spec.md         # Track specification (Specification) — classic FR list or story-shaped
│       └── plan.md         # Implementation plan (Implementation Plan)
└── archive/                # Completed/archived tracks

# Optional, at project root (TS projects only):
graph.db                    # build-graph SQLite knowledge graph — enables Graph-Aware Mode
```

## Commands

### Setup
Initialize Measure in a new or existing project. For TypeScript projects, §2.9 offers to install `build-graph` and scaffold a knowledge graph (enables Graph-Aware Mode across new-track, implement, and review). Read [references/setup.md](references/setup.md) for the full workflow.

### New Track
Create a new track with spec and plan. Offers a choice between **Story-shaped spec** (recommended for features — Connextra + Gherkin AC + T-shirt size + priority) and **Classic FR list** (recommended for bugs/chores). When Graph-Aware Mode is available, runs a Graph Context Probe before questioning and appends blast-radius notes to plan phases. Read [references/new-track.md](references/new-track.md) for the full workflow.

### Implement
Execute tasks from a track's plan following the project workflow. Loads project memory (lessons learned, tech debt) before starting, loads graph baseline when Graph-Aware Mode is available, applies a Per-Task Graph Protocol around exported-symbol edits, and prompts for retrospective insights before finalizing. Read [references/implement.md](references/implement.md) for the full workflow.

### Review
Review completed work against product guidelines, code styleguides, and the original plan. Checks for recurring gotchas from lessons learned. When Graph-Aware Mode is available, runs `build-graph callers` for every changed exported symbol and flags High-severity findings for un-updated callers of non-additive signature changes. Read [references/review.md](references/review.md) for the full workflow.

### Doctor (/measure:doctor)
Run architectural linting and structural checks on the repository (e.g., boundary enforcement, generated doc freshness) to prevent context drift and junk-drawer coding. Read [references/doctor.md](references/doctor.md) for the full workflow.

### Status
Display project progress overview including track breakdown, project health indicators, and (for projects with completed feature tracks) a rolling velocity and estimation-accuracy ratio. Read [references/status.md](references/status.md) for the full workflow.

### Revert
Roll back previous work by track, phase, or task using Git history. Read [references/revert.md](references/revert.md) for the full workflow.

## Task Status Markers

- `[ ]` - Pending
- `[~]` - In Progress
- `[x]` - Completed

## Key Principles

1. **Plan is Source of Truth**: All work tracked in `plan.md`
2. **Test-Driven Development**: Write tests before implementation
3. **High Code Coverage**: Target >80%
4. **Atomic Commits**: Commit after each task
5. **Git Notes**: Attach task summaries for auditability

## Assets

- **Workflow Template**: [assets/workflow.md](assets/workflow.md)
- **Code Styleguides**: [assets/code_styleguides/](assets/code_styleguides/)
- **Lessons Learned Template**: [assets/lessons-learned.md](assets/lessons-learned.md)
- **Tech Debt Template**: [assets/tech-debt.md](assets/tech-debt.md)

# Skill: measure-orchestrator

# Measure Orchestrator

Use this skill to turn a Measure track into a coordinated sequence of focused subagents. The Measure subagents (`measure-strategy`, `measure-mid-red`, `measure-jr-green`, `measure-review-a-correctness`, `measure-review-b-security`, `measure-review-c-ux-api`, `measure-phase-acceptance`, `measure-adversarial-testing`, `measure-ux-browser-review`, `measure-final-acceptance`, `measure-closeout`, `measure-orchestrator-audit`) are already registered as opencode subagent types — invoke them with the `task` tool's `subagent_type` parameter. `scripts/measure_interphase_checks.py` provides mechanical checks between handoffs.

## Anti-Patterns Registry

Every project that uses the orchestrator should have a `measure/anti-patterns.md` that
catalogs orchestrator anti-patterns caught in that project or in the framework. The
catalog uses an A1–AN naming scheme; the orchestrator's auditors and reviewers consult
it before passing phase acceptance. A starter catalog with 10 entries (A1–A10) lives at
`references/anti-pattern-catalog.md` in this skill; projects extend it with project-
specific entries as they catch new classes of failure. The `measure-orchestrator-audit`
subagent appends new entries to project `measure/anti-patterns.md` when it catches a
new class of failure that the framework doesn't yet cover.

## Marker Vocabulary (Standardized)

Every plan uses these three markers:

- `[x]` — complete
- `[~]` — in-progress (live implementation; AI or human is working on it)
- `[b]` — blocked / human-gated (with trailing `deferred:<owner>` field)

The legacy `[ ]` (space) marker is **deprecated**. Some plans still use it for
"deferred" or "not started" but the supervisor no longer treats space as in-progress
(supervisor regex is `r"^- \[([~xb])\] (.+)"`). When a plan has `[ ]` (space) markers,
reclassify them to `[b]` with `deferred:<owner>` per the verification-checkpoint rule.

The supervisor's `is_task_structurally_blocked(task)` helper in
`measure/automation-supervisor.py` recognizes:
- `[b]` checkbox state
- trailing `deferred:<owner>` field (e.g. `… — deferred:phikul`)

A free-text occurrence of the word "deferred" no longer drops a task from the
incomplete count (this is **anti-pattern A1**, the highest-priority orchestrator
anti-pattern; see `references/anti-pattern-catalog.md`).

## `tests/_lib/` Template (deferred — see `tech-debt.md`)

A future template will provide shared bash libraries for every contract test to source:

- `banned_re.sh` — extracts `BANNED_RE` from `measure/doctor.sh` and prints it
- `track_dir.sh` — `track_dir_resolve <id>` prefers `measure/archive/<id>` if it exists
- `marker_consistency.sh` — `marker_consistency_check <plan> <phase>` returns INCOMPLETE on
  a phase with 0 `[x]` tasks (anti-pattern A4)
- `consent_check.sh` — `consent_check <artifact>` returns OK if anonymized or consent
  artifact present (anti-pattern A2)
- `refutation_filter.sh` — `refutation_filter <input>` excludes only file-path contexts
  and policy-disclaimer markers, not bare English words (anti-pattern A7)

The full lib is deferred (large change). Until installed, each `tests/*.sh` re-implements
the patterns inline; the `measure-orchestrator-audit` subagent flags divergence.

## Aggregate `bash measure/test-all.sh` (lightweight, post-deferred-lib)

Until the lib is installed, projects can add a `bash measure/test-all.sh` aggregate that:

- runs every `tests/*.sh` (no glob skip; tests that opt out of aggregates use a
  `## skip-aggregate:` header per test-strategy.md §7)
- emits a single summary: total tests, total PASS, total FAIL, exit code
- is the canonical "run every measure contract test" entry point

This replaces the current `npm test` (which only runs `tests/s1.sh` on TUTOR-001
projects). A future pre-commit hook can run this aggregate.

## Start Here

1. Find the Measure repo root. It must contain `measure/index.md`, `measure/tracks.md`,
   `measure/anti-patterns.md`, and `measure/tracks/`.
2. Read `measure/index.md`, `measure/tracks.md`, `measure/anti-patterns.md`, the
   selected track `spec.md`, the selected track `plan.md`, and `test-strategy.md` if
   present.
3. Run:

```bash
python3 ~/.agents/skills/measure-orchestrator/scripts/measure_interphase_checks.py status --repo .
```

Use the first listed incomplete phase as the default next phase unless the user names a
track or phase. **Note:** a phase with 0 non-deferred incomplete tasks is reported as
"all phases complete" — but this can mean "all automatable work done, humans need to do
the rest." Verify `[b]` markers in the plan are intentional before declaring success.

## Role Order

Run roles in this order. Strategy, Mid, and Jr are sequential. Review A/B/C can run in
parallel after Jr commits Green work if their write scopes are clear. The audit role
runs at any point in the cycle (recommended: weekly + on every supervisor change). Final
Acceptance must pass before Closeout.

1. `measure-strategy`
2. `measure-mid-red`
3. `measure-jr-green`
4. `measure-review-a-correctness`
5. `measure-review-b-security`
6. `measure-review-c-ux-api`
7. `measure-phase-acceptance`
8. `measure-adversarial-testing`
9. `measure-ux-browser-review` when applicable
10. `measure-orchestrator-audit` (anytime; recommended after every supervisor change)
11. `measure-final-acceptance`
12. `measure-closeout`

The `measure-orchestrator-audit` role is the only one that audits the *framework* itself
(supervisor, test scripts, plan truthfulness). Other audit roles audit the
*implementation* of a specific track. The two are complementary.

## Delegation

Invoke each role by calling the `task` tool with `subagent_type` set to the matching
Measure subagent type (e.g. `measure-jr-green`, `measure-mid-red`, `measure-review-a-correctness`,
`measure-orchestrator-audit`). Pass these values in the task prompt:

- repo root (absolute path)
- track id
- phase heading (or "track setup" / "track review" where appropriate)
- baseline SHA (`git rev-parse HEAD` at role start)
- result JSON path for audit roles (where the audit JSON must be written)
- relevant gate commands from the environment (`RED_TEST_COMMAND`, `GREEN_TEST_COMMAND`,
  `PROJECT_LINT`, `PROJECT_CHECKS`, `PROJECT_TESTS`, `PROJECT_DEV_URL`)

Every subagent may edit, because reviewers and auditors are expected to fix proven
blockers before returning. Preserve unrelated user work and do not revert changes made by
other agents.

## Inter-Phase Checks

Run the checker after each role. Treat failures as feedback for the next attempt.

```bash
python3 ~/.agents/skills/measure-orchestrator/scripts/measure_interphase_checks.py role-gate --repo . --role mid-red --track TRACK --phase "Phase 2: Test" --baseline BASE_SHA --log-file LOG
python3 ~/.agents/skills/measure-orchestrator/scripts/measure_interphase_checks.py role-gate --repo . --role phase-acceptance --track TRACK --phase "Phase 2: Test" --baseline BASE_SHA --result-file RESULT.json --log-file LOG
python3 ~/.agents/skills/measure-orchestrator/scripts/measure_interphase_checks.py closeout --repo . --track TRACK
```

The checker intentionally fails when required configured gates are missing. Set:

- `RED_TEST_COMMAND` for Mid.
- `GREEN_TEST_COMMAND` for Jr.
- `PROJECT_LINT`, `PROJECT_CHECKS`, and `PROJECT_TESTS` for final acceptance.
- `PROJECT_DEV_URL` when UX browser review is applicable.
- `UX_REQUIRED=auto|always|never`.

## Contracts

Read `references/contracts.md` before writing or reviewing role prompts. It defines the
required `MEASURE_AGENT_RESULT` block and audit JSON shape.

## Closeout Standard

Do not archive a track just because a markdown artifact says it passed. Closeout must verify:

- no non-deferred plan tasks remain (no `[~]`, no `[ ]` — only `[x]` or `[b]` with
  `deferred:<owner>`)
- completed tasks include commit SHA evidence
- final acceptance audit passed
- `measure/tracks/<track>` was moved to `measure/archive/<track>`
- `measure/tracks.md` no longer lists the track in the active section
- `metadata.json` has `status: "done"` and a completion date
- `automation-supervisor-closeout-manifest.json` exists
- no anti-pattern anti-A5 (false-claim text) or anti-A6 (registry overstatement) is
  present in `plan.md` or `measure/tracks.md`

## Evaluation

Initial eval prompts live at `evals/evals.json`. Before declaring the skill finished, run
the skill-creator evaluation loop and generate the human review artifact with
`eval-viewer/generate_review.py`. The 4th eval prompt (added in this revision) probes
the audit subagent's detection of A1–A7 anti-patterns.

Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.

1: # Project Workflow
2: 
3: ## Guiding Principles
4: 
5: 1. **The Plan is the Source of Truth:** All work must be tracked in `plan.md`
6: 2. **The Tech Stack is Deliberate:** Changes to the tech stack must be documented in `tech-stack.md` *before* implementation
7: 3. **Test-Driven Development:** Write unit tests before implementing functionality
8: 4. **High Code Coverage:** Aim for >80% code coverage for all modules
9: 5. **User Experience First:** Every decision should prioritize user experience
10: 6. **Non-Interactive & CI-Aware:** Prefer non-interactive commands. Use `CI=true` for watch-mode tools (tests, linters) to ensure single execution.
11: 
12: ## Task Workflow
13: 
14: All tasks follow a strict lifecycle:
15: 
16: ### Standard Task Workflow
17: 
18: 1. **Select Task:** Choose the next available task from `plan.md` in sequential order
19: 
20: 2. **Mark In Progress:** Before beginning work, edit `plan.md` and change the task from `[ ]` to `[~]`
21: 
22: 3. **Write Failing Tests (Red Phase):**
23:    - Create a new test file for the feature or bug fix.
24:    - Write one or more unit tests that clearly define the expected behavior and acceptance criteria for the task.
25:    - **CRITICAL:** Run the tests and confirm that they fail as expected. This is the "Red" phase of TDD. Do not proceed until you have failing tests.
26: 
27: 4. **Implement to Pass Tests (Green Phase):**
28:    - Write the minimum amount of application code necessary to make the failing tests pass.
29:    - Run the test suite again and confirm that all tests now pass. This is the "Green" phase.
30: 
31: 5. **Refactor (Optional but Recommended):**
32:    - With the safety of passing tests, refactor the implementation code and the test code to improve clarity, remove duplication, and enhance performance without changing the external behavior.
33:    - Rerun tests to ensure they still pass after refactoring.
34: 
35: 6. **Verify Coverage:** Run coverage reports using the project's chosen tools. For example, in a Python project, this might look like:
36:    ```bash
37:    pytest --cov=app --cov-report=html
38:    ```
39:    Target: >80% coverage for new code. The specific tools and commands will vary by language and framework.
40: 
41: 7. **Document Deviations:** If implementation differs from tech stack:
42:    - **STOP** implementation
43:    - Update `tech-stack.md` with new design
44:    - Add dated note explaining the change
45:    - Resume implementation
46: 
47: 8. **Log Known Shortcuts as Tech Debt:** If a shortcut was knowingly taken during implementation (e.g., skipping an edge case, hardcoding a value, deferring error handling), prompt the user: "A shortcut was taken. Would you like to add a row to `tech-debt.md`?" If yes, append a row with the date, track ID, description, severity, and `Open` status. Check line count with `wc -l` first; if `tech-debt.md` exceeds 50 lines, ask the user to prune resolved items before adding new ones.
48: 
49: 9. **Commit Code Changes:**
50:    - Stage all code changes related to the task.
51:    - Propose a clear, concise commit message e.g, `feat(ui): Create basic HTML structure for calculator`.
52:    - Perform the commit.
53: 
54: 10. **Attach Task Summary with Git Notes:**
55:     - **Step 10.1: Get Commit Hash:** Obtain the hash of the *just-completed commit* (`git log -1 --format="%H"`).
56:     - **Step 10.2: Draft Note Content:** Create a detailed summary for the completed task. This should include the task name, a summary of changes, a list of all created/modified files, and the core "why" for the change.
57:     - **Step 10.3: Attach Note:** Use the `git notes` command to attach the summary to the commit.
58:       ```bash
59:       # The note content from the previous step is passed via the -m flag.
60:       git notes add -m "<note content>" <commit_hash>
61:       ```
62: 
63: 11. **Get and Record Task Commit SHA:**
64:     - **Step 11.1: Update Plan:** Read `plan.md`, find the line for the completed task, update its status from `[~]` to `[x]`, and append the first 7 characters of the *just-completed commit's* commit hash.
65:     - **Step 11.2: Write Plan:** Write the updated content back to `plan.md`.
66: 
67: 12. **Commit Plan Update:**
68:     - **Action:** Stage the modified `plan.md` file.
69:     - **Action:** Commit this change with a descriptive message (e.g., `measure(plan): Mark task 'Create user model' as complete`).
70: 
71: ### Phase Completion Verification and Checkpointing Protocol
72: 
73: **Trigger:** This protocol is executed immediately after a task is completed that also concludes a phase in `plan.md`.
74: 
75: 1.  **Announce Protocol Start:** Inform the user that the phase is complete and the verification and checkpointing protocol has begun.
76: 
77: 2.  **Ensure Test Coverage for Phase Changes:**

# Project Workflow

## Guiding Principles

1. **The Plan is the Source of Truth:** All work must be tracked in `plan.md`

3. **Test-Driven Development:** Write unit tests before implementing functionality
4. **High Code Coverage:** Aim for >80% code coverage for all modules
5. **User Experience First:** Every decision should prioritize user experience
6. **Non-Interactive & CI-Aware:** Prefer non-interactive commands. Use `CI=true` for watch-mode tools (tests, linters) to ensure single execution.

## Task Workflow

All tasks follow a strict lifecycle:

### Standard Task Workflow

1. **Select Task:** Choose the next available task from `plan.md` in sequential order

2. **Mark In Progress:** Before beginning work, edit `plan.md` and change the task from `[ ]` to `[~]`

3. **Write Failing Tests (Red Phase):**
   - Create a new test file for the feature or bug fix.
   - Write one or more unit tests that clearly define the expected behavior and acceptance criteria for the task.
   - **CRITICAL:** Run the tests and confirm that they fail as expected. This is the "Red" phase of TDD. Do not proceed until you have failing tests.

4. **Implement to Pass Tests (Green Phase):**
   - Write the minimum amount of application code necessary to make the failing tests pass.
   - Run the test suite again and confirm that all tests now pass. This is the "Green" phase.

5. **Refactor (Optional but Recommended):**
   - With the safety of passing tests, refactor the implementation code and the test code to improve clarity, remove duplication, and enhance performance without changing the external behavior.
   - Rerun tests to ensure they still pass after refactoring.

6. **Verify Coverage:** Run coverage reports using the project's chosen tools. For example, in a Python project, this might look like:
   ```bash
   pytest --cov=app --cov-report=html
   ```
   Target: >80% coverage for new code. The specific tools and commands will vary by language and framework.

7. **Document Deviations:** If implementation differs from tech stack:
   - **STOP** implementation
   - Update `tech-stack.md` with new design
   - Add dated note explaining the change
   - Resume implementation

8. **Log Known Shortcuts as Tech Debt:** If a shortcut was knowingly taken during implementation (e.g., skipping an edge case, hardcoding a value, deferring error handling), prompt the user: "A shortcut was taken. Would you like to add a row to `tech-debt.md`?" If yes, append a row with the date, track ID, description, severity, and `Open` status. Check line count with `wc -l` first; if `tech-debt.md` exceeds 50 lines, ask the user to prune resolved items before adding new ones.

9. **Commit Code Changes:**
   - Stage all code changes related to the task.
   - Propose a clear, concise commit message e.g, `feat(ui): Create basic HTML structure for calculator`.
   - Perform the commit.

10. **Attach Task Summary with Git Notes:**
    - **Step 10.1: Get Commit Hash:** Obtain the hash of the *just-completed commit* (`git log -1 --format="%H"`).
    - **Step 10.2: Draft Note Content:** Create a detailed summary for the completed task. This should include the task name, a summary of changes, a list of all created/modified files, and the core "why" for the change.
    - **Step 10.3: Attach Note:** Use the `git notes` command to attach the summary to the commit.
      ```bash
      # The note content from the previous step is passed via the -m flag.
      git notes add -m "<note content>" <commit_hash>
      ```

11. **Get and Record Task Commit SHA:**
    - **Step 11.1: Update Plan:** Read `plan.md`, find the line for the completed task, update its status from `[~]` to `[x]`, and append the first 7 characters of the *just-completed commit's* commit hash.
    - **Step 11.2: Write Plan:** Write the updated content back to `plan.md`.

12. **Commit Plan Update:**
    - **Action:** Stage the modified `plan.md` file.
    - **Action:** Commit this change with a descriptive message (e.g., `measure(plan): Mark task 'Create user model' as complete`).

### Phase Completion Verification and Checkpointing Protocol

**Trigger:** This protocol is executed immediately after a task is completed that also concludes a phase in `plan.md`.

1.  **Announce Protocol Start:** Inform the user that the phase is complete and the verification and checkpointing protocol has begun.

2.  **Ensure Test Coverage for Phase Changes:**

    -   **Step 2.2: List Changed Files:** Execute `git diff --name-only <previous_checkpoint_sha> HEAD` to get a precise list of all files modified during this phase.
    -   **Step 2.3: Verify and Create Tests:** For each file in the list:
        -   **CRITICAL:** First, check its extension. Exclude non-code files (e.g., `.json`, `.md`, `.yaml`).
        -   For each remaining code file, verify a corresponding test file exists.
        -   If a test file is missing, you **must** create one. Before writing the test, **first, analyze other test files in the repository to determine the correct naming convention and testing style.** The new tests **must** validate the functionality described in this phase's tasks (`plan.md`).

3.  **Execute Automated Tests with Proactive Debugging:**

     -   **Example Announcement:** "I will now run the automated test suite to verify the phase. **Command:** `CI=true npm test`"

     -   If tests fail, you **must** inform the user and begin debugging. You may attempt to propose a fix a **maximum of two times**. If the tests still fail after your second proposed fix, you **must stop**, report the persistent failure, and ask the user for guidance.

     -   **Step 4.1: Determine Review Scope:** Identify the revision range for this phase. Use the Git commit SHA of the *previous* phase's checkpoint (from `plan.md`) as the base. If no previous checkpoint exists, use the first commit in the track.
     -   **Step 4.2: Spawn Review Subagent:** Launch a `change-quality-reviewer` subagent to review the diff for the phase. The subagent prompt **must** include:

        3.  **Confirm that you receive:** A JSON response with a status of `201 Created`.
        ```

6.  **Await Explicit User Feedback:**
     -   After presenting the detailed plan, ask the user for confirmation: "**Does this meet your expectations? Please confirm with yes or provide feedback on what needs to be changed.**"
     -   **PAUSE** and await the user's response. Do not proceed without an explicit yes or confirmation.

7.  **Create Checkpoint Commit:**
     -   Stage all changes. If no changes occurred in this step, proceed with an empty commit.

8.  **Attach Auditable Verification Report using Git Notes:**

     -   **Step 9.2: Update Plan:** Read `plan.md`, find the heading for the completed phase, and append the first 7 characters of the commit hash in the format `[checkpoint: <sha>]`.
     -   **Step 9.3: Write Plan:** Write the updated content back to `plan.md`.

10. **Commit Plan Update:**
    - **Action:** Stage the modified `plan.md` file.
    - **Action:** Commit this change with a descriptive message following the format `measure(plan): Mark phase '<PHASE NAME>' as complete`.

5. Code passes all configured linting and static analysis checks
6. Works beautifully on mobile (if applicable)
7. Implementation notes added to `plan.md`
8. Changes committed with proper message
9. Git note with task summary attached to the commit

## Emergency Procedures

### Critical Bug in Production
1. Create hotfix branch from main
2. Write failing test for bug
3. Implement minimal fix
4. Test thoroughly including mobile
5. Deploy immediately
6. Document in plan.md

### Data Loss
1. Stop all write operations
2. Restore from latest backup
3. Verify data integrity
4. Document incident
5. Update backup procedures

### Security Breach
1. Rotate all secrets immediately
2. Review access logs
3. Patch vulnerability
4. Notify affected users (if any)
5. Document and update security procedures

## Deployment Workflow

### Pre-Deployment Checklist
- [ ] All tests passing
- [ ] Coverage >80%
- [ ] No linting errors
- [ ] Mobile testing complete
- [ ] Environment variables configured
- [ ] Database migrations ready
- [ ] Backup created

### Deployment Steps
1. Merge feature branch to main
2. Tag release with version
3. Push to deployment service
4. Run database migrations
5. Verify deployment
6. Test critical paths
7. Monitor for errors

### Post-Deployment
1. Monitor analytics
2. Check error logs
3. Gather user feedback
4. Plan next iteration

## Continuous Improvement

- Review workflow weekly
- Update based on pain points
- Document lessons learned
- Optimize for user happiness
- Keep things simple and maintainable

37: 
38: ## A1 — Substring-as-structured-signal in supervisor
39: 
40: **Class:** orchestrator heuristic bypass
41: **Caught:** 2026-06-24 review of last-72h commits vs. measure phase state
42: **Detection:**
43: ```bash
44: # Use Python to strip docstrings before matching (the false-positive on docstring
45: # mentions is itself a known failure mode of grep-based detection).
46: python3 -c '
47: import re
48: src = open("measure/automation-supervisor.py").read()
49: code = re.sub(r"\"\"\".*?\"\"\"", "", src, flags=re.DOTALL)
50: code = re.sub(r"'"'"'.*?'"'"'", "", code, flags=re.DOTALL)
51: matches = re.findall(r"\"deferred\"[[:space:]]+in[[:space:]]+task\.lower\(\)", code)
52: print(len(matches), "substring-match occurrences")
53: '
54: ```
55: 
56: **Symptoms:** A `[~]` task with the substring "deferred" in its prose is silently dropped
57: from the incomplete-task count. Tracks can mark a task `[~]` *without* doing the work
58: and the supervisor still reports "complete."
59: 
60: **Fix:** Replace the substring check with a structured-signal helper
61: (`is_task_structurally_blocked(task)` in `measure/automation-supervisor.py`) that
62: recognizes:
63: - `[b]` (blocked / human-gated) checkbox state
64: - trailing `deferred:<owner>` field
65: 
66: A free-text occurrence of "deferred" no longer drops a task from the incomplete count.
67: 
68: **Guard:** `tests/orchestrator_supervisor_invariants.sh`.
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## A2 — Consent-blind publish gate
73: 
74: **Class:** orchestrator missing requirement
75: **Caught:** 2026-06-24 review
76: **Detection:**
77: ```bash
78: for t in tests/*p4.sh tests/*_closeout.sh tests/cs_p*.sh; do
79:   if [ -f "$t" ]; then
80:     n=$(grep -ic 'consent\|anonym' "$t" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
81:     echo "$t: $n consent/anonymization references"
82:     [ "$n" = "0" ] && echo "  WARN: publish gate has no consent or anonymization check"
83:   fi
84: done
85: ```
86: 
87: **Symptoms:** A test that flips a draft → published status does not check for consent
88: artifacts or anonymization. A named case study can be published without consent
89: verification.
90: 
91: **Fix:** For any "publish" gate in `tests/*p4.sh` or `tests/*_closeout.sh`, the gate must
92: require EITHER (a) explicit anonymization marker on the artifact, OR (b) a non-empty
93: `consent-<subject>.{md,pdf}` artifact with signatory + date.
94: 
95: **Guard:** none (no active publish gate currently uses this pattern; orchestrator audit required).
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## A3 — Digit-only as a "labeled count"
100: 
101: **Class:** test fragility / vacuous assertion
102: **Caught:** 2026-06-24 review
103: **Detection:**
104: ```bash
105: rg -n "rg -q '\[0-9\]\+'" tests/*.sh
106: ```
107: 
108: **Symptoms:** A test asserts a "count" or "baseline" with a regex that matches any digit
109: (`rg -q '[0-9]+'`). The test passes on a date, a year, or any digit anywhere in the
110: section.
111: 
112: **Fix:** Require a labeled integer — `rg 'Baseline relationship count:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+'`
113: and parse the integer.
114: 
115: **Guard:** none (orchestrator audit required).
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## A4 — Vacuous-pass on nothing-done
120: 
121: **Class:** test fragility / vacuous assertion
122: **Caught:** 2026-06-24 review
123: **Detection:**
124: ```bash
125: for t in tests/mr_p{1..4}.sh; do
126:   if [ -f "$t" ]; then
127:     pair=$(awk '
128:       /TILDES=/ && /-eq 0/ { t=1 }
129:       t && /XES=/ && /-eq 0/ { found=1; exit }
130:       END { print found+0 }
131:     ' "$t")
132:     [ "$pair" = "1" ] && echo "  $t: vacuous 'markers consistent' PASS"
133:   fi
134: done
135: ```
136: 
137: **Symptoms:** A "markers consistent" check passes when a phase has zero completed tasks
138: (all-`[~]`) AND when a phase has zero in-progress tasks (all-`[x]`). A phase reporting
139: "Green" with no `[x]` is inflated to a passing check.
140: 
141: **Fix:** Reclassify the all-`[~]` state as `INCOMPLETE` (and `FAIL` the test), reserve
142: `PASS` for "all-`[x]`" (with `>= 1 [x]`).
143: 
144: **Guard:** none (orchestrator audit required).
145: 
146: ---
147: 
148: ## A5 — False-claim text vs test reality
149: 
150: **Class:** plan truthfulness
151: **Caught:** 2026-06-24 review
152: **Detection:**
153: ```bash
154: rg -n "PASS=[0-9]+.*FAIL=0|all checks pass" measure/tracks/*/plan.md
155: # For each hit, run the test the plan cites; if exit != 0, the claim is false.
156: ```
157: 
158: **Symptoms:** A plan task claims "all checks pass" or "PASS=6, FAIL=0" while the test
159: the plan cites actually exits 1.
160: 
161: **Fix:** When a test invariant is incompatible with a spec requirement, either retire
162: the test in favor of a new one or update the test. Do not write "all checks pass" in
163: plan text unless the test actually exits 0.
164: 
165: **Guard:** none (orchestrator audit required).
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ## A6 — Registry-note overstatement
170: 
171: **Class:** marketing copy outrunning implementation
172: **Caught:** 2026-06-24 review
173: **Detection:**
174: ```bash
175: rg -n "API-key encryption (was )?resolved|encryption.*resolved|completely fixed|fully solved|all (checks |tests )?pass" measure/tracks.md
176: # For each hit, check the corresponding adversarial test or contract test is green.
177: ```
178: 
179: **Symptoms:** A registry note or `measure/tracks.md` entry claims a security/quality
180: state is "resolved" while the adversarial test for that state is still failing.
181: 
182: **Fix:** When an adversarial test is red, the registry note must say so. A claim of
183: "resolved" is only valid when the adversarial test passes.
184: 
185: **Guard:** none (orchestrator audit required).
186: 
187: ---
188: 
189: ## A7 — Over-broad filter swallowing real hits
190: 
191: **Class:** test filter too coarse
192: **Caught:** 2026-06-24 review
193: **Detection:**
194: ```bash
195: rg -n 'rg -v "[^"]*(never|do not|do NOT|don.t|cannot say|forbidden|prohibited)[^"]*"' tests/*.sh
196: ```
197: 
198: **Symptoms:** A test's exclusion filter uses bare English words ("never", "do not",
199: "don't") as filter tokens. A real banned-term line that happens to contain "never"
200: gets silently dropped.
201: 
202: **Fix:** Exclude only file path contexts and policy-disclaimer markers
203: (`outcome-claims-policy.md`, `❌`, `BANNED`), not bare English words.
204: 
205: **Guard:** none (orchestrator audit required).
206: 
207: ---
208: 
209: ## A8 — `[ ]` (space) marker ambiguity (legacy)
210: 
211: **Class:** supervisor regex accepts too many markers
212: **Caught:** 2026-06-24 review (post-supervisor fix)
213: **Detection:**
214: ```bash
215: rg -n 'r"\^\- \[\(\[ ~x\]\)\]' measure/automation-supervisor.py
216: ```
217: 
218: **Symptoms:** The supervisor's task regex `r"^- \[([ ~x])\] (.+)"` accepts a space
219: character. A `[ ]` (space) marker is counted as in-progress.
220: 
221: **Fix:** Standardize on `r"^- \[([~xb])\] (.+)"`; the supervisor's incomplete-count
222: predicate should be `status in ("~", "b") and not is_task_structurally_blocked(task)`.
223: Project plans that still use `[ ]` must be converted by the plan-update role before
224: supervisor execution, because the fixed supervisor intentionally ignores `[ ]` tasks.
225: 
226: **Guard:** `tests/orchestrator_marker_vocabulary.sh` for planning-review tracks; static supervisor regex check in `measure-orchestrator-audit`.
227: 
228: ---
229: 
230: ## A9 — Pre-existing test references archived track paths
231: 
232: **Class:** test not updated on archive move
233: **Caught:** Multiple occurrences after archive moves
234: **Detection:**
235: ```bash
236: rg -n 'measure/tracks/([a-z_0-9-]+)/plan\.md' tests/*.sh
237: # Cross-check: for each track id, if measure/archive/<id>/ exists and measure/tracks/<id>/ doesn't, the test is broken.
238: ```
239: 
240: **Symptoms:** A test references `measure/tracks/<id>/plan.md` but the track was moved
241: to `measure/archive/<id>/plan.md` on closeout. The test fails forever.
242: 
243: **Fix:** Add a `track_dir_resolve()` helper at the top of every test that prefers
244: `measure/archive/<id>` if it exists. A shared helper remains deferred.
245: 
246: **Guard:** Static check in `measure-orchestrator-audit`.
247: 
248: ---
249: 
250: ## A10 — Generated-facts drift after structural change
251: 
252: **Class:** CI gate that fights developers
253: **Caught:** Every `measure/doctor.sh` Check 5 failure
254: **Detection:**
255: ```bash
256: ls -la .git/hooks/pre-commit 2>/dev/null
257: ```
258: 
259: **Symptoms:** `measure/doctor.sh` Check 5 fails after every structural change because
260: no pre-commit hook regenerates `measure/generated/`.
261: 
262: **Fix:** Add a pre-commit hook that runs `bash measure/generate.sh` and stages the
263: result.
264: 
265: **Guard:** Static check in `measure-orchestrator-audit`.
266: 
267: ---
268: 
269: ## A11 — Executed review track left fully blocked
270: 
271: **Class:** plan truthfulness / supervisor bypass
272: **Caught:** 2026-06-27 orchestrator audit for `reading_advantage_full_review_20260626`
273: 
274: **Detection:**
275: ```bash
276: # For a review track with review result JSON and/or audit-report artifacts, the plan must
277: # not leave every task as `[b] ... deferred:review-execution`.
278: for plan in measure/tracks/*/plan.md; do
279:   dir="${plan%/plan.md}"
280:   if ls "$dir"/review-*-result.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
281:     total=$(grep -c '^- \[[~xb]\] ' "$plan" || true)
282:     blocked=$(grep -c '^- \[b\].*deferred:review-execution' "$plan" || true)
283:     if [ "$total" -gt 0 ] && [ "$total" = "$blocked" ]; then
284:       echo "WARN: executed review track still fully blocked: $plan"
285:     fi
286:   fi
287: done
288: ```
289: 
290: **Symptoms:** Review result artifacts exist and the user has requested execution, but the
291: track plan still marks every task as `[b] ... deferred:review-execution`. Because `[b]`
292: is a structured blocked marker, the supervisor treats the track as having no executable
293: work. The plan then stops representing current truth: execution happened or is authorized,
294: but task markers still say it is human-gated.
295: 
296: **Fix:** Once execution is requested or review artifacts exist, convert task markers to
297: truthful states: `[x]` for completed tasks with artifact/result evidence, `[~]` for
298: remaining executable tasks, or keep `[b] deferred:<owner>` only for a real external gate.
299: Do not use `[b] deferred:review-execution` as a permanent placeholder after execution
300: begins.
301: 
302: **Guard:** `tests/orchestrator_review_execution_truthfulness.sh`.
303: 
304: ---
305: 
306: ## A12 — Dangling catalog guard-references (unguarded anti-patterns)
307: 
308: **Class:** catalog / guard drift
309: **Caught:** 2026-07-03 orchestrator audit
310: 
311: **Detection:**
312: ```bash
313: # Every "Guard: tests/<name>.sh" reference in this catalog must point at a file
314: # that actually exists. The starter catalog referenced track-specific guards
315: # (`mir_p1.sh`, `cs_p4.sh`, and `mr_p*.sh`) that were never created in
316: # this repo, so A1-A7 were silently unguarded.
317: for ref in $(grep -oE 'tests/[a-z_0-9]+\.sh' measure/anti-patterns.md | sort -u); do
318:   [ -f "$ref" ] || echo "DANGLING guard reference: $ref"
319: done
320: ```
321: 
322: **Symptoms:** The catalog's per-entry `Guard:` line names a test file that does
323: not exist in the repo. Readers (and the orchestrator) believe A1-A7 are guarded
324: when they are not. A regression of A1 (substring-as-signal) or A3 (digit-only
325: count) would not be caught by any test, only by a manual orchestrator audit.
326: 
327: **Fix:** Either (a) create the referenced guard test, or (b) update the
328: `Guard:` line to `none (... — see A12)` and rely on the orchestrator audit.
329: This repo chose (b) for A2-A7 (low-frequency in current tracks) and (a) for A1
330: and A8 via `tests/orchestrator_supervisor_invariants.sh` and the expanded
331: `tests/orchestrator_marker_vocabulary.sh`.
332: 
333: **Guard:** `tests/orchestrator_catalog.sh` enforces that every A-entry exists;
334: the dangling-reference sweep itself is run by the orchestrator audit (no static
335: guard yet).
336: 
337: ---
338: 
339: ## A13 — Stale track directory left in `measure/tracks/` after archive move
340: 
341: **Class:** closeout / registry drift
342: **Caught:** 2026-07-03 orchestrator audit of `agents_md_audit_science_advantage_20260603`
343: 
344: **Detection:**
345: ```bash
346: # A track that tracks.md marks archived (link under ./archive/) must NOT also
347: # have a directory under measure/tracks/. A stale leftover means the active
348: # track list is inconsistent with the registry.
349: for d in measure/tracks/*/; do
350:   tid=$(basename "$d")
351:   if grep -q "\./archive/${tid}/" measure/tracks.md && [ ! -f "${d}plan.md" ]; then
352:     echo "STALE: $tid is archived in tracks.md but a dir remains in measure/tracks/ (no plan.md)"
353:   fi
354: done
355: ```
356: 
357: **Symptoms:** `tracks.md` marks a track `[x]` archived with a `./archive/<id>/`
358: link, and `measure/archive/<id>/` holds the complete archived track, BUT a
359: leftover `measure/tracks/<id>/` directory still exists (often with only stray
360: fixtures and no `plan.md`/`metadata.json`). The active-track enumeration and the
361: registry disagree. Because the leftover has no `plan.md`, the marker-vocabulary
362: guard skips it silently, so the drift is invisible.
363: 
364: **Fix:** `measure-closeout` must remove the `measure/tracks/<id>/` directory
365: once the archive move is complete and verified (archive copy has `plan.md`,
366: `metadata.json`, and all artifacts). Do not leave stray fixtures behind.
367: 
368: **Guard:** Orchestrator audit (no static guard yet).
369: 
370: ---
371: 
372: ## A14 — Invalid ripgrep option makes detectors non-executable
373: 
374: **Class:** audit detector vacuity / command portability
375: **Caught:** 2026-07-12 Phase 0 orchestrator audit
376: 
377: **Detection:**
378: ```bash
379: # ripgrep uses Rust-regex syntax by default; `-E` means `--encoding`, unlike grep.
380: # `rg -nE '<regex>' ...` therefore consumes the regex as an encoding name and exits 2.
381: rg -n -- 'rg -nE' measure/anti-patterns.md
382: ```
383: 
384: **Symptoms:** A catalog recipe copied from `grep -E` uses `rg -nE`. Ripgrep reports
385: `unknown encoding`, and a wrapper ending the command with `|| true` turns the detector
386: failure into apparent zero findings. A1–A13 can then be reported clean without having
387: executed their regexes.
388: 
389: **Fix:** Use `rg -n '<regex>' ...` because ripgrep already enables its regular-expression
390: engine by default. Treat detector exit 2 as an audit failure; do not collapse it into a
391: zero-hit result.
392: 
393: **Guard:** `tests/orchestrator_detector_syntax.sh`.
394: 
395: ---
396: 
397: ## A15 — Stale role-receipt hashes after reviewed fixes
398: 
399: **Class:** provenance drift / unverifiable role output
400: **Caught:** 2026-07-12 Phase 0 orchestrator audit of
401: `measure_apk_evidence_integrity_gates_20260712`
402: 
403: **Detection:**
404: ```bash
405: bash tests/orchestrator_role_receipt_integrity.sh
406: ```
407: 
408: **Symptoms:** A role receipt enumerates output-file SHA-256 values, then Green or review
409: fixes modify those files without refreshing or superseding the receipt. The receipt still
410: looks complete but no longer attests to the bytes at HEAD, so role provenance and output
411: ownership cannot honestly be accepted.
412: 
413: **Fix:** Preserve the original receipt as an immutable receipt for its exact commit, and
414: publish a new tool-attested receipt for every later role/fix commit. Each receipt must bind
415: the real event IDs, role identity, commit, final response, and current output hashes; do
416: not rewrite placeholders into retrospective claims.
417: 
418: **Guard:** `tests/orchestrator_role_receipt_integrity.sh`.
419: 
420: ---
421: 
422: ## How projects extend this catalog
423: 
424: When a new class of failure is caught (in this project, in another project, or by the
425: `measure-orchestrator-audit` subagent):
426: 
427: 1. Add a new entry to the project's `measure/anti-patterns.md` (or to this canonical
428:    file if it's framework-wide).
429: 2. Use a unique A-number (continue from the highest existing entry).
430: 3. Provide: description, detection recipe, symptoms, fix, and a guard test reference.
431: 4. The `measure-orchestrator-audit` subagent will pick up the new entry in its next run.
432: 
433: ## Cross-project propagation
434: 
435: When a new A-entry is added to a project's `measure/anti-patterns.md`, the
436: `measure-orchestrator-audit` subagent reports the entry as a "promotion candidate" in
437: its audit result. The orchestrator's Mid + Jr cycle can then promote the entry to
438: `references/anti-pattern-catalog.md` so all projects benefit.

(End of file - total 438 lines)
</content>

verification.

**Fix:** For any "publish" gate in `tests/*p4.sh` or `tests/*_closeout.sh`, the gate must
require EITHER (a) explicit anonymization marker on the artifact, OR (b) a non-empty
`consent-<subject>.{md,pdf}` artifact with signatory + date.

**Guard:** none (no active publish gate currently uses this pattern; orchestrator audit required).

---

## A3 — Digit-only as a "labeled count"

**Class:** test fragility / vacuous assertion
**Caught:** 2026-06-24 review
**Detection:**
```bash
rg -n "rg -q '\[0-9\]\+'" tests/*.sh
```

**Symptoms:** A test asserts a "count" or "baseline" with a regex that matches any digit
(`rg -q '[0-9]+'`). The test passes on a date, a year, or any digit anywhere in the
section.

**Fix:** Require a labeled integer — `rg 'Baseline relationship count:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+'`
and parse the integer.

**Guard:** none (orchestrator audit required).

---

## A4 — Vacuous-pass on nothing-done

**Class:** test fragility / vacuous assertion
**Caught:** 2026-06-24 review
**Detection:**
```bash
for t in tests/mr_p{1..4}.sh; do
  if [ -f "$t" ]; then
    pair=$(awk '
      /TILDES=/ && /-eq 0/ { t=1 }
      t && /XES=/ && /-eq 0/ { found=1; exit }
      END { print found+0 }
    ' "$t")
    [ "$pair" = "1" ] && echo "  $t: vacuous 'markers consistent' PASS"
  fi
done
```

**Symptoms:** A "markers consistent" check passes when a phase has zero completed tasks
(all-`[~]`) AND when a phase has zero in-progress tasks (all-`[x]`). A phase reporting
"Green" with no `[x]` is inflated to a passing check.

**Fix:** Reclassify the all-`[~]` state as `INCOMPLETE` (and `FAIL` the test), reserve
`PASS` for "all-`[x]`" (with `>= 1 [x]`).

**Guard:** none (orchestrator audit required).

---

## A5 — False-claim text vs test reality

**Class:** plan truthfulness
**Caught:** 2026-06-24 review
**Detection:**
```bash
rg -n "PASS=[0-9]+.*FAIL=0|all checks pass" measure/tracks/*/plan.md
# For each hit, run the test the plan cites; if exit != 0, the claim is false.
```

**Symptoms:** A plan task claims "all checks pass" or "PASS=6, FAIL=0" while the test
the plan cites actually exits 1.

**Fix:** When a test invariant is incompatible with a spec requirement, either retire
the test in favor of a new one or update the test. Do not write "all checks pass" in
plan text unless the test actually exits 0.

**Guard:** none (orchestrator audit required).

---

## A6 — Registry-note overstatement

**Class:** marketing copy outrunning implementation
**Caught:** 2026-06-24 review
**Detection:**
```bash
rg -n "API-key encryption (was )?resolved|encryption.*resolved|completely fixed|fully solved|all (checks |tests )?pass" measure/tracks.md
# For each hit, check the corresponding adversarial test or contract test is green.
```

**Symptoms:** A registry note or `measure/tracks.md` entry claims a security/quality
state is "resolved" while the adversarial test for that state is still failing.

**Fix:** When an adversarial test is red, the registry note must say so. A claim of
"resolved" is only valid when the adversarial test passes.

**Guard:** none (orchestrator audit required).

---

## A7 — Over-broad filter swallowing real hits

**Class:** test filter too coarse
**Caught:** 2026-06-24 review
**Detection:**
```bash
rg -n 'rg -v "[^"]*(never|do not|do NOT|don.t|cannot say|forbidden|prohibited)[^"]*"' tests/*.sh
```

**Symptoms:** A test's exclusion filter uses bare English words ("never", "do not",
"don't") as filter tokens. A real banned-term line that happens to contain "never"
gets silently dropped.

**Fix:** Exclude only file path contexts and policy-disclaimer markers
(`outcome-claims-policy.md`, `❌`, `BANNED`), not bare English words.

**Guard:** none (orchestrator audit required).

---

## A8 — `[ ]` (space) marker ambiguity (legacy)

**Class:** supervisor regex accepts too many markers
**Caught:** 2026-06-24 review (post-supervisor fix)
**Detection:**
```bash
rg -n 'r"\^\- \[\(\[ ~x\]\)\]' measure/automation-supervisor.py
```

**Symptoms:** The supervisor's task regex `r"^- \[([ ~x])\] (.+)"` accepts a space
character. A `[ ]` (space) marker is counted as in-progress.

**Fix:** Standardize on `r"^- \[([~xb])\] (.+)"`; the supervisor's incomplete-count
predicate should be `status in ("~", "b") and not is_task_structurally_blocked(task)`.
Project plans that still use `[ ]` must be converted by the plan-update role before
supervisor execution, because the fixed supervisor intentionally ignores `[ ]` tasks.

**Guard:** `tests/orchestrator_marker_vocabulary.sh` for planning-review tracks; static supervisor regex check in `measure-orchestrator-audit`.

---

## A9 — Pre-existing test references archived track paths

**Class:** test not updated on archive move
**Caught:** Multiple occurrences after archive moves
**Detection:**
```bash
rg -n 'measure/tracks/([a-z_0-9-]+)/plan\.md' tests/*.sh
# Cross-check: for each track id, if measure/archive/<id>/ exists and measure/tracks/<id>/ doesn't, the test is broken.
```

**Symptoms:** A test references `measure/tracks/<id>/plan.md` but the track was moved
to `measure/archive/<id>/plan.md` on closeout. The test fails forever.

**Fix:** Add a `track_dir_resolve()` helper at the top of every test that prefers
`measure/archive/<id>` if it exists. A shared helper remains deferred.

**Guard:** Static check in `measure-orchestrator-audit`.

---

## A10 — Generated-facts drift after structural change

**Class:** CI gate that fights developers
**Caught:** Every `measure/doctor.sh` Check 5 failure
**Detection:**
```bash
ls -la .git/hooks/pre-commit 2>/dev/null
```

**Symptoms:** `measure/doctor.sh` Check 5 fails after every structural change because
no pre-commit hook regenerates `measure/generated/`.

**Fix:** Add a pre-commit hook that runs `bash measure/generate.sh` and stages the
result.

**Guard:** Static check in `measure-orchestrator-audit`.

---

## A11 — Executed review track left fully blocked

**Class:** plan truthfulness / supervisor bypass
**Caught:** 2026-06-27 orchestrator audit for `reading_advantage_full_review_20260626`

**Detection:**
```bash
# For a review track with review result JSON and/or audit-report artifacts, the plan must
# not leave every task as `[b] ... deferred:review-execution`.
for plan in measure/tracks/*/plan.md; do
  dir="${plan%/plan.md}"
  if ls "$dir"/review-*-result.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    total=$(grep -c '^- \[[~xb]\] ' "$plan" || true)
    blocked=$(grep -c '^- \[b\].*deferred:review-execution' "$plan" || true)
    if [ "$total" -gt 0 ] && [ "$total" = "$blocked" ]; then
      echo "WARN: executed review track still fully blocked: $plan"
    fi
  fi
done
```

**Symptoms:** Review result artifacts exist and the user has requested execution, but the
track plan still marks every task as `[b] ... deferred:review-execution`. Because `[b]`
is a structured blocked marker, the supervisor treats the track as having no executable
work. The plan then stops representing current truth: execution happened or is authorized,
but task markers still say it is human-gated.

**Fix:** Once execution is requested or review artifacts exist, convert task markers to
truthful states: `[x]` for completed tasks with artifact/result evidence, `[~]` for
remaining executable tasks, or keep `[b] deferred:<owner>` only for a real external gate.
Do not use `[b] deferred:review-execution` as a permanent placeholder after execution
begins.

**Guard:** `tests/orchestrator_review_execution_truthfulness.sh`.

---

## A12 — Dangling catalog guard-references (unguarded anti-patterns)

**Class:** catalog / guard drift
**Caught:** 2026-07-03 orchestrator audit

**Detection:**
```bash
# Every "Guard: tests/<name>.sh" reference in this catalog must point at a file
# that actually exists. The starter catalog referenced track-specific guards
# (`mir_p1.sh`, `cs_p4.sh`, and `mr_p*.sh`) that were never created in
# this repo, so A1-A7 were silently unguarded.
for ref in $(grep -oE 'tests/[a-z_0-9]+\.sh' measure/anti-patterns.md | sort -u); do
  [ -f "$ref" ] || echo "DANGLING guard reference: $ref"
done
```

**Symptoms:** The catalog's per-entry `Guard:` line names a test file that does
not exist in the repo. Readers (and the orchestrator) believe A1-A7 are guarded
when they are not. A regression of A1 (substring-as-signal) or A3 (digit-only
count) would not be caught by any test, only by a manual orchestrator audit.

**Fix:** Either (a) create the referenced guard test, or (b) update the
`Guard:` line to `none (... — see A12)` and rely on the orchestrator audit.
This repo chose (b) for A2-A7 (low-frequency in current tracks) and (a) for A1
and A8 via `tests/orchestrator_supervisor_invariants.sh` and the expanded
`tests/orchestrator_marker_vocabulary.sh`.

**Guard:** `tests/orchestrator_catalog.sh` enforces that every A-entry exists;
the dangling-reference sweep itself is run by the orchestrator audit (no static
guard yet).

---

## A13 — Stale track directory left in `measure/tracks/` after archive move

**Class:** closeout / registry drift
**Caught:** 2026-07-03 orchestrator audit of `agents_md_audit_science_advantage_20260603`

**Detection:**
```bash
# A track that tracks.md marks archived (link under ./archive/) must NOT also
# have a directory under measure/tracks/. A stale leftover means the active
# track list is inconsistent with the registry.
for d in measure/tracks/*/; do
  tid=$(basename "$d")
  if grep -q "\./archive/${tid}/" measure/tracks.md && [ ! -f "${d}plan.md" ]; then
    echo "STALE: $tid is archived in tracks.md but a dir remains in measure/tracks/ (no plan.md)"
  fi
done
```

**Symptoms:** `tracks.md` marks a track `[x]` archived with a `./archive/<id>/`
link, and `measure/archive/<id>/` holds the complete archived track, BUT a
leftover `measure/tracks/<id>/` directory still exists (often with only stray
fixtures and no `plan.md`/`metadata.json`). The active-track enumeration and the
registry disagree. Because the leftover has no `plan.md`, the marker-vocabulary
guard skips it silently, so the drift is invisible.

**Fix:** `measure-closeout` must remove the `measure/tracks/<id>/` directory
once the archive move is complete and verified (archive copy has `plan.md`,
`metadata.json`, and all artifacts). Do not leave stray fixtures behind.

**Guard:** Orchestrator audit (no static guard yet).

---

## A14 — Invalid ripgrep option makes detectors non-executable

**Class:** audit detector vacuity / command portability
**Caught:** 2026-07-12 Phase 0 orchestrator audit

**Detection:**
```bash
# ripgrep uses Rust-regex syntax by default; `-E` means `--encoding`, unlike grep.
# `rg -nE '<regex>' ...` therefore consumes the regex as an encoding name and exits 2.
rg -n -- 'rg -nE' measure/anti-patterns.md
```

**Symptoms:** A catalog recipe copied from `grep -E` uses `rg -nE`. Ripgrep reports
`unknown encoding`, and a wrapper ending the command with `|| true` turns the detector
failure into apparent zero findings. A1–A13 can then be reported clean without having
executed their regexes.

**Fix:** Use `rg -n '<regex>' ...` because ripgrep already enables its regular-expression
engine by default. Treat detector exit 2 as an audit failure; do not collapse it into a
zero-hit result.

**Guard:** `tests/orchestrator_detector_syntax.sh`.

---

## A15 — Stale role-receipt hashes after reviewed fixes

**Class:** provenance drift / unverifiable role output
**Caught:** 2026-07-12 Phase 0 orchestrator audit of
`measure_apk_evidence_integrity_gates_20260712`

**Detection:**
```bash
bash tests/orchestrator_role_receipt_integrity.sh
```

**Symptoms:** A role receipt enumerates output-file SHA-256 values, then Green or review
fixes modify those files without refreshing or superseding the receipt. The receipt still
looks complete but no longer attests to the bytes at HEAD, so role provenance and output
ownership cannot honestly be accepted.

**Fix:** Preserve the original receipt as an immutable receipt for its exact commit, and
publish a new tool-attested receipt for every later role/fix commit. Each receipt must bind
the real event IDs, role identity, commit, final response, and current output hashes; do
not rewrite placeholders into retrospective claims.

**Guard:** `tests/orchestrator_role_receipt_integrity.sh`.

---

## How projects extend this catalog

When a new class of failure is caught (in this project, in another project, or by the
`measure-orchestrator-audit` subagent):

1. Add a new entry to the project's `measure/anti-patterns.md` (or to this canonical
   file if it's framework-wide).
2. Use a unique A-number (continue from the highest existing entry).
3. Provide: description, detection recipe, symptoms, fix, and a guard test reference.
4. The `measure-orchestrator-audit` subagent will pick up the new entry in its next run.

## Cross-project propagation

When a new A-entry is added to a project's `measure/anti-patterns.md`, the
`measure-orchestrator-audit` subagent reports the entry as a "promotion candidate" in
its audit result. The orchestrator's Mid + Jr cycle can then promote the entry to
`references/anti-pattern-catalog.md` so all projects benefit.

Reject directories, generated prose as primary evidence, stale hashes, unreachable revisions, and inference presented as fact.

### FR2: Independent denominator validation

Define denominator item and reconciliation schemas. Authored requirement outputs cannot supply their own completeness denominator.

### FR3: Role independence

Define tool-attested role receipts and per-task ownership manifests. 370: 
371:     @param messages Validated session messages.
372:     @param message_id Expected provider message identifier.
373:     @returns Matching message, or ``None`` when absent or duplicated.
374:     """
375:     matches = [message for message in messages if message.get("info", {}).get("id") == message_id]
376:     return matches[0] if len(matches) == 1 else None

379: def _resolve_trusted_export(
380:     resolver: TrustedSessionResolver, session_id: Any
381: ) -> Mapping[str, Any] | None:
382:     """Resolves and parses one session exclusively through a trusted provider adapter.
383: 
384:     @param resolver Trusted live provider boundary.
385:     @param session_id Session identifier declared by retained evidence.
386:     @returns Parsed live export, or ``None`` when resolution fails closed.
387:     """
388:     if not isinstance(session_id, str):
389:         return None
390:     try:
391:         value = json.loads(resolver.resolve(session_id))
392:     except (OSError, RuntimeError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
393:         return None
394:     return value if isinstance(value, Mapping) else None

397: def _validate_trusted_event_snapshots(
398:     retained_export: Mapping[str, Any],
399:     *,
400:     resolver: TrustedSessionResolver,
401:     session_id: Any,
402:     parent_session_id: Any | None,
403:     agent: Any,
404:     event_ids: tuple[Any, ...],
405:     require_full_history: bool = False,
406: ) -> bool:
407:     """Compares retained evidence with trusted live provider exports.
408: 
409:     @param retained_export Locally retained export already bound by content hashes.
410:     @param resolver Trusted live provider boundary.
411:     @param session_id Expected session identity.
412:     @param parent_session_id Expected parent session identity.
413:     @param agent Expected session agent identity.
414:     @param event_ids Exact provider event IDs that must match.
415:     @param require_full_history Whether the complete canonical message sequence must match.
416:     @returns Whether live session identity and required history exactly match retention.
417:     """
418:     live_export = _resolve_trusted_export(resolver, session_id)
419:     if live_export is None:
420:         return False
421:     retained_messages = _validated_export_messages(
422:         retained_export, session_id=session_id, parent_session_id=parent_session_id
423:     )
424:     live_messages = _validated_export_messages(
425:         live_export, session_id=session_id, parent_session_id=parent_session_id
426:     )
427:     retained_info = retained_export.get("info")
428:     live_info = live_export.get("info")
429:     if (
430:         retained_messages is None
431:         or live_messages is None
432:         or not isinstance(retained_info, Mapping)
433:         or not isinstance(live_info, Mapping)
434:         or retained_info.get("agent") != agent
435:         or live_info.get("agent") != agent
436:     ):
437:         return False
438:     identity_fields = ("id", "parentID", "agent", "fork_turns")
439:     if (
440:         {field: retained_info.get(field) for field in identity_fields}
441:         != {field: live_info.get(field) for field in identity_fields}
442:         or (
443:             require_full_history
444:             and _canonical_json({"messages": retained_messages})
445:             != _canonical_json({"messages": live_messages})
446:         )
447:     ):
448:         return False
449:     for event_id in event_ids:
450:         retained_event = _message_by_id(retained_messages, event_id)
451:         live_event = _message_by_id(live_messages, event_id)
452:         if (
453:             retained_event is None
454:             or live_event is None
455:             or _canonical_json(retained_event) != _canonical_json(live_event)
456:         ):
457:             return False
458:     return True
459:

461: def _validate_review_provenance(
462:     repo: Path,
463:     review: Mapping[str, Any],
464:     *,
465:     candidate_hash: Any,
466:     candidate: Mapping[str, Any],
467:     gate_commit: Any,
468:     gate_version: Any,
469:     trusted_resolver: TrustedSessionResolver | None = None,
470: ) -> tuple[bool, int | None]:
471:     """Validates retained reviewer identity and provider-neutral context isolation.
472: 
473:     @param repo Resolved repository root.
474:     @param review Bound independent-review report.
475:     @param candidate_hash Exact candidate manifest hash.
476:     @param candidate Parsed candidate manifest.
477:     @param gate_commit Reviewed implementation commit.
478:     @param gate_version Reviewed gate version.
479:     @param trusted_resolver Explicit trusted live provider resolver.
480:     @returns Validation result and provider completion timestamp.
481:     """
482:     provenance = review.get("fresh_context_provenance")
483:     if not isinstance(provenance, Mapping) or provenance.get("role") != "adversarial-reviewer":
484:         return False, None
485:     export = _load_bound_raw_export(
486:         repo,
487:         provenance.get("raw_export_path"),
488:         provenance.get("raw_export_sha256"),
489:         provenance.get("stored_export_sha256"),
490:     )
491:     if export is None:
492:         return False, None
493:     if trusted_resolver is None or not _validate_trusted_event_snapshots(
494:         export,
495:         resolver=trusted_resolver,
496:         session_id=provenance.get("session_id"),
497:         parent_session_id=provenance.get("parent_session_id"),
498:         agent=provenance.get("agent"),
499:         event_ids=(
500:             provenance.get("prompt_message_id"),
501:             provenance.get("final_response_message_id"),
502:         ),
503:         require_full_history=True,
504:     ):
505:         return False, None
506:     messages = _validated_export_messages(
507:         export,
508:         session_id=provenance.get("session_id"),
509:         parent_session_id=provenance.get("parent_session_id"),
510:     )
511:     if messages is None:
512:         return False, None
513:     prompt = _message_by_id(messages, provenance.get("prompt_message_id"))
514:     final = _message_by_id(messages, provenance.get("final_response_message_id"))
515:     if prompt is None or final is None:
516:         return False, None
517:     prompt_info = prompt.get("info", {})
518:     final_info = final.get("info", {})
519:     final_time = final_info.get("time", {})
520:     completed = final_time.get("completed")
521:     assistants = [message for message in messages if message.get("info", {}).get("role") == "assistant"]
522:     reviewer_users = [message for message in messages if message.get("info", {}).get("role") == "user"]
523:     explicit_none = export.get("info", {}).get(
524:         "fork_turns", export.get("fork_turns")
525:     ) == "none"
526:     equivalent_fresh_history = (
527:         provenance.get("isolation_proof") == "raw-history-begins-with-fresh-prompt"
528:         and messages[0] is prompt
529:     )
530:     expected_prompt = _canonical_json({
531:         "candidate_manifest_sha256": candidate_hash,
532:         "gate_version": gate_version,
533:         "implementation_commit": gate_commit,
534:         "source_base_commit": candidate.get("source_base_commit"),
535:         "task": "independent-adversarial-review",
536:     })
537:     expected_final = _canonical_json({
538:         "candidate_manifest_sha256": candidate_hash,
539:         "review_status": review.get("review_status"),
540:         "unresolved_findings": review.get("unresolved_findings"),
541:     })
542:     valid = bool(
543:         prompt_info.get("role") == "user"
544:         and export.get("info", {}).get("agent") == provenance.get("agent")
545:         and final_info.get("role") == "assistant"
546:         and final_info.get("parentID") == provenance.get("prompt_message_id")
547:         and final is assistants[-1]
548:         and assistants
549:         and reviewer_users == [prompt]
550:         and all(
551:             message.get("info", {}).get("parentID") == provenance.get("prompt_message_id")
552:             for message in assistants
553:         )
554:         and {message.get("info", {}).get("agent") for message in assistants}
555:         == {provenance.get("agent")}
556:         and _sha256_bytes(_message_text_bytes(prompt)) == provenance.get("prompt_text_sha256")
557:         and _sha256_bytes(_message_text_bytes(final))
558:         == provenance.get("final_response_text_sha256")
559:         and prompt_info.get("time", {}).get("created") == provenance.get("started_ms")
560:         and isinstance(completed, int)
561:         and completed == provenance.get("completed_ms")
562:         and _message_text_bytes(prompt) == expected_prompt
563:         and _message_text_bytes(final) == expected_final
564:         and messages[0] is prompt
565:         and (explicit_none or equivalent_fresh_history)
566:     )
567:     return valid, completed if valid else None
568:

570: def _validate_owner_provenance(
571:     repo: Path,
572:     approval: Mapping[str, Any],
573:     *,
574:     candidate_hash: Any,
575:     review_hash: Any,
576:     gate_commit: Any,
577:     gate_version: Any,
578:     review_completed_ms: int,
579:     trusted_resolver: TrustedSessionResolver | None = None,
580: ) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
581:     """Validates retained owner approval, root designation, bindings, and ordering.
582: 
583:     @param repo Resolved repository root.
584:     @param approval Bound owner-approval artifact.
585:     @param candidate_hash Exact candidate artifact hash.
586:     @param review_hash Exact independent-review artifact hash.
587:     @param gate_commit Reviewed gate implementation commit.
588:     @param gate_version Reviewed gate version.
589:     @param review_completed_ms Provider timestamp when review completed.
590:     @param trusted_resolver Explicit trusted live provider resolver.
591:     @returns Validation result and the approval event ID for replay protection.
592:     """
593:     event = approval.get("approval_event")
594:     root = approval.get("root_owner_delegation")
595:     if not isinstance(event, Mapping) or not isinstance(root, Mapping):
596:         return False, None
597:     export = _load_bound_raw_export(
598:         repo,
599:         event.get("raw_export_path"),
600:         event.get("raw_export_sha256"),
601:         event.get("stored_export_sha256"),
602:     )
603:     root_export = _load_bound_raw_export(
604:         repo,
605:         root.get("raw_export_path"),
606:         root.get("raw_export_sha256"),
607:         root.get("stored_export_sha256"),
608:     )
609:     if export is None or root_export is None:
610:         return False, None
611:     messages = _validated_export_messages(
612:         export,
613:         session_id=event.get("session_id"),
614:         parent_session_id=event.get("parent_session_id"),
615:     )
616:     root_messages = _validated_export_messages(
617:         root_export, session_id=root.get("session_id"), parent_session_id=None
618:     )
619:     if messages is None or root_messages is None:
620:         return False, None
621:     prompt = _message_by_id(messages, event.get("prompt_message_id"))
622:     designation_contract = root.get("owner_designation_event")
623:     publication_contract = root.get("approval_publication_event")
624:     if (
625:         prompt is None
626:         or not isinstance(designation_contract, Mapping)
627:         or not isinstance(publication_contract, Mapping)
628:     ):
629:         return False, None
630:     if trusted_resolver is None or not _validate_trusted_event_snapshots(
631:         export,
632:         resolver=trusted_resolver,
633:         session_id=event.get("session_id"),
634:         parent_session_id=event.get("parent_session_id"),
635:         agent=event.get("agent"),
636:         event_ids=(event.get("prompt_message_id"),),
637:     ) or not _validate_trusted_event_snapshots(
638:         root_export,
639:         resolver=trusted_resolver,
640:         session_id=root.get("session_id"),
641:         parent_session_id=None,
642:         agent=root.get("agent"),
643:         event_ids=(
644:             designation_contract.get("message_id"),
645:             publication_contract.get("message_id"),
646:         ),
647:     ):
648:         return False, None
649:     designation = _message_by_id(root_messages, designation_contract.get("message_id"))
650:     publication = _message_by_id(root_messages, publication_contract.get("message_id"))
651:     if designation is None or publication is None:
652:         return False, None
653:     prompt_bytes = _message_text_bytes(prompt)
654:     prompt_created = prompt.get("info", {}).get("time", {}).get("created")
655:     designation_created = designation.get("info", {}).get("time", {}).get("created")
656:     publication_created = publication.get("info", {}).get("time", {}).get("created")
657:     expected_prompt = _canonical_json({
658:         "candidate_manifest_sha256": candidate_hash,
659:         "decision": "approve",
660:         "gate_commit": gate_commit,
661:         "gate_version": gate_version,
662:         "review_report_sha256": review_hash,
663:     })
664:     task_parts = [
665:         part
666:         for part in publication.get("parts", [])
667:         if isinstance(part, Mapping)
668:         and part.get("type") == "tool"
669:         and part.get("tool") == "task"
670:         and part.get("callID") == publication_contract.get("task_call_id")
671:     ]
672:     task_state = task_parts[0].get("state") if len(task_parts) == 1 else None
673:     task_input = task_state.get("input") if isinstance(task_state, Mapping) else None
674:     task_metadata = task_state.get("metadata") if isinstance(task_state, Mapping) else None
675:     approval_assistants = [
676:         message for message in messages if message.get("info", {}).get("role") == "assistant"
677:     ]
678:     valid = bool(
679:         event.get("role") == "product-owner"
680:         and export.get("info", {}).get("agent") == event.get("agent")
681:         and root_export.get("info", {}).get("agent") == root.get("agent")
682:         and prompt.get("info", {}).get("role") == "user"
683:         and messages[0] is prompt
684:         and approval_assistants
685:         and {message.get("info", {}).get("agent") for message in approval_assistants}
686:         == {event.get("agent")}
687:         and _sha256_bytes(prompt_bytes) == event.get("prompt_text_sha256")
688:         and prompt_created == event.get("prompt_created_ms")
689:         and isinstance(prompt_created, int)
690:         and prompt_created > review_completed_ms
691:         and prompt_bytes == expected_prompt
692:         and designation.get("info", {}).get("role") == "user"
693:         and _message_text_bytes(designation) == OWNER_DELEGATION_TEXT
694:         and designation_contract.get("designated_role") == "product-owner"
695:         and designation_contract.get("delegate_agent") == event.get("agent")
696:         and _sha256_bytes(_message_text_bytes(designation))
697:         == designation_contract.get("message_text_sha256")
698:         and designation_created == designation_contract.get("created_ms")
699:         and publication_created == publication_contract.get("created_ms")
700:         and publication.get("info", {}).get("role") == "assistant"
701:         and publication.get("info", {}).get("agent") == root.get("agent")
702:         and isinstance(designation_created, int)
703:         and isinstance(publication_created, int)
704:         and designation_created < publication_created < prompt_created
705:         and isinstance(task_input, Mapping)
706:         and isinstance(task_metadata, Mapping)
707:         and task_state.get("status") == "completed"
708:         and task_metadata.get("sessionId") == event.get("session_id")
709:         and task_metadata.get("parentSessionId") == root.get("session_id")
710:         and task_metadata.get("sessionId") == publication_contract.get("delegated_session_id")
711:         and _sha256_bytes(str(task_input.get("prompt", "")).encode())
712:         == publication_contract.get("delegated_prompt_sha256")
713:         == _sha256_bytes(prompt_bytes)
714:     )
715:     return valid, event.get("prompt_message_id") if valid else None
716:
